extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, chymists, and experimental scientists (17th-century and historians of science)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating claims about the elementary composition of bodies derived from experimental analyses (especially those using fire or solvent 'menstruums'), and assessing whether analytic products are genuine pre-existing principles or artifacts of the method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume the fire is a universal and sufficient analyzer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fire is not an Universal Analyzer of all Mixt Bodies; it is not necessarily an adæquate and sufficient instrument to analyze mixt Bodies with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand explicit demonstration before asserting that fire alone divides a compound into its true 'hypostatical Principles'. Consider counter-evidence where fire fails to separate metals/minerals into purported elementary principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider alternative analytic agents and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: There may be other Bodies or Ways which will as well as the Fire divide Concretes into several homogeneous Substances (e.g., Helmont's Alkahest or other Menstruums); Nature or Art may provide instruments that analyze differently from fire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating analytic claims, explore whether non-thermal methods (solvents, gentle heat, mechanical separation, cold, biological processes) produce different or more genuine separations; do not treat fire-based analysis as the default or only valid method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require evidence that separated substances were pre-existent in the body
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not so sure that every Seemingly Similar or Distinct Substance that is Separated from a Body by the Help of the Fire, was Pre existent in it as a Principle or Element of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between material pre-existence and forms produced during analysis. Insist on arguments (beyond mere separation) that a given fraction existed in that form in the original material rather than being formed de novo by the analytic process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish extraction from chemical coalition when using additaments
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Menstruum or other Additament is employ'd, examine whether it does barely help to separate the Principle obtain'd, or whether there intervene not a coalition of the parts of the Body wrought upon with those of the Menstruum, whereby the produc'd Concrete may be judg'd to result from the Union of both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design controls to test whether solvents/reactants are inert extractors or chemically participate; avoid treating products obtained with reagents as necessarily intrinsic to the original sample without demonstrating no reagent-derived contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer direct observation and replication
rubrics_metrics.description: He that hath seen it hath more Reason to beleeve it, than He that hath not; witness and personal trial strengthen belief in surprising experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give greater weight to claims backed by direct, reproducible observations and credible eye-witness testimony; request demonstrations or independent replications for extraordinary experimental claims (e.g., universal dissolvents, volatile salts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for volatility and containment to avoid loss or artifact
rubrics_metrics.description: Volatile components (e.g., 'inflammable spirit') may fly away unless vessels are carefully stopt; distillation in open or poorly stopped apparatus can give misleading results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate containment (stopped vessels, receivers) and procedural controls to prevent evaporation losses and ensure collected fractions reflect what was in the sample rather than artifacts of escape or exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret fractionation in terms of physical properties, not necessarily elementary identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fire often separates parts because some are more fixt and some more volatile; the apparent congregation/segregation (congregare homogenea & heterogenea segregare) may be accidental, arising from differences in volatility, gravity, or texture rather than true elementary distinctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before concluding that fractions correspond to true 'principles', analyze whether separation can be explained by differential volatility, density, or texture. Avoid equating physical fractionation order directly with elemental composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize heating can produce unions or new stable compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fire sometimes does not Separate, so much as Unite, Bodies of a differing Nature (vitrification, fusion, formation of new fixed bodies); violent heat can create new, inseparable combinations rather than reveal pre-existing parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to thermal artifacts (e.g., vitrification, amalgams, new sublimates) that are products of the analytic heat itself. Use gentler methods or complementary analyses to detect such artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require multiple lines of argument beyond analysis results to claim elementary status
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be Rational to suspect that Chymists may deceive themselves in concluding resolutely and universally that substances separated by analysis are elementary; at least till some other argument than that drawn from the Analysis be brought to resolve the Doubt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims of elemental status with independent evidence (chemical reactivity, reproducible isolation by varied methods, theoretical justification), not solely with the fact of separation by a single analytic method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use careful, repeatable experimental procedure and adequate controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental results (e.g., freeze separations, distillations, weight measurements) often vary with conditions; single or poorly controlled trials can mislead (e.g., freezing of wines/urine not always producing separations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct replicated trials, control environmental variables (degree of cold, vessel sealing, timing), and avoid generalizing from single instances. Report procedural details (temperatures, sealing, timing) so others can reproduce results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative measurement and verification of mass/constitutive changes
rubrics_metrics.description: In plant/soil trials, weighing soil before and after growth and repeated drying can indicate whether mass changes are due to moisture or substantive loss/transformations; check for alternate explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply quantitative methods (weighing, repeated drying) and consider mechanical loss (dust, handling) when interpreting mass differences. Use proper controls to attribute mass change to biological uptake vs experimental artifacts.
